summary: Two small corrections: the meta-analysis's first author is Romain Ghibellini, not Riccardo, and Zeigarnik's first experiment used 18 to 22 tasks per person, not exactly 22. Everything else checked out, including every quotation.

changes.after: A 2025 meta-analysis by Romain Ghibellini and Beat Meier
changes.why: The first author's name is Romain Ghibellini (University of Bern).

changes.why: Zeigarnik's own paper says each subject was given 'from 18 to 22 tasks'. MacLeod's review rounds this to 22.

notes: Three links could not be opened directly because my tools were refused access to them: the Springer PDF of MacLeod (2020) and the two doi.org links. I read the same papers through other copies (MacLeod's lab copy at uwaterloo.ca and the University of Bern copy of the meta-analysis) and confirmed both DOIs are correct from independent records, but I have not seen those three links load. The PubMed page opened but showed no text to my tools; I confirmed the abstract, including the quoted sentence, from a library catalogue record.

The two waiter stories (Boring 1957, MacKinnon in Marrow 1969) differ, as the story says. MacLeod reports Lewin's 1933 Moscow visit and Zeigarnik telling him of Hitler; Andrey Zeigarnik's memoir confirms the visit but doesn't mention Hitler.
Ovsiankina's emigration year differs between sources (1931 or 1938); the story gives no year.
